tables.name: adult_nasal_linear_norms_naw
tables.population: Young adult North American White (Farkas-type caliper norms) as carried in this library; not a single verified source
tables.notes: Expert ranges consistent with anthropometric-norms.md Table values; al-al means consistent with doubling the sourced alare-midline values (PMC12500730). Population-unknown fits should widen al-al sigma to ~4 mm. Verify against Farkas 1994.

tables.name: sourced_nasal_width_measurements
rows: Southern Spain European adults, normal occlusion
tables.notes: Each row is single-source from harvest summaries. Malay width is much larger than typical al-al and may use a different landmark definition (contested).

tables.name: nasal_skeleton_measurements
tables.notes: Sourced rows reused from anatomy/skull-osteology.md. Aperture predicts external nose poorly (PMC7527952: 26 of 76 relations significant; PMC10557396: RV < 0.4); use only as a soft consistency check.

tables.name: profile_angles_and_projection_ratios
rows: n'-prn dorsal line vs facial plane g'-pg'
alar-cheek junction to tip / radix to tip
radix in front of corneal plane / radix to tip
tables.population: Rhinoplasty aesthetic references, derived mostly from European-descent 'attractive' samples; population means differ
tables.notes: Goode, Crumley and nasofacial angle encode one right triangle (asin(0.55-0.60) = 33-37 deg); use only one as a prior. Use aesthetic values as UI warnings (weight <= 0.1 of population prior). Definitions of nasolabial angle vary and shift values by up to ~10 deg. Verify against Powell & Humphreys 1984, Byrd & Hobar 1993, Crumley & Lanser 1988.

tables.name: nasal_soft_tissue_cover
rows: pooled review; Iranian MRI range across BMI groups (low to high BMI)
tables.notes: Men thicker at nasion and rhinion (PMC3762959) and in nasal region (pubmed 41701465). Hard floor for fitting: skin >= 1.5 mm over nasal bones. BMI slope smallest on the nasal dorsum.

tables.name: nasal_index_classes_living
tables.notes: Cut-offs differ between authors and between skull and living-nose indices; some schemes add hyperleptorrhine and hyperplatyrrhine classes.

tables.name: perspective_magnification_nose
tables.units: ratio (d + delta) / d; d = camera to nose tip in m
tables.notes: Pure point-depth magnification; clinical selfie-effect reports (~30% wider nasal base at 12 in vs 5 ft, Ward et al. 2018) exceed geometry, likely via occluding-contour shift and width definitions. Perspective depends on distance, not focal length (practitioner sources digitaltrends.com, photographylife.com).

tables.name: pose_error_nose
rows: pitch: prn vertical shift vs n' and alar base
tables.notes: Use midline points for profile ratios; alar points move with yaw. Half-width 16 mm from sourced alare-midline 15.4-17.3 mm.

tables.name: nose_fit_priors
tables.notes: Engine design defaults, not measured norms. Landmark observation sigma (library landmark-detection.md): prn 2.5% IOD, sn 1.5% IOD; allow 1-2 mm prn bias toward specular highlight. Hard constraints: skin >= 1.5 mm over nasal bones; ac 8-16 mm behind sn; columella below alar rim.

tables.name: detector_index_map_nose
tables.notes: dlib nose block is sourced by two tutorials; individual index-to-anatomy mappings and all MediaPipe indices are from library notes (craniometric-landmarks.md, landmark-detection.md) and need verification. Detector 'alar' points sit near ac/sbal, not anatomical al.
